svg.title: Agent Sandbox Implementation Options and Security Controls
svg.desc: An expanded implementation map covering application controls, virtual shells, OS process sandboxes, containers, sandboxed kernels and microVMs, remote execution, Agent security governance, WASM runtimes, persistent workspaces, and browser isolation. Projects are mapped to their actual boundaries and required security policies.
svg.text: Expanded project map · implementation boundary, concrete stacks, and security policy obligations
SECURITY POLICIES TO CONFIGURE AND VERIFY
Not an OS boundary for arbitrary
code running in the host process.
FUSE-backed filesystem projection · none / view / read / write access levels
Expose only projected paths; distinguish directory visibility from content reads; enforce writes at the filesystem layer;
test symlink, mount, rename and platform filesystem behavior. Do not treat a FUSE view as process isolation.
Separate Read / Write / Edit tools · Virtual Filesystem · scoped path permissions · pluggable execute backend
Default deny; independently authorize read, write, delete and execute; bind approval to exact diff / digest / target;
stage and version changes; keep script creation separate from script execution; audit each decision.
Scoped filesystem server · directory handles · resource identifiers and constrained operations
Resolve paths safely; prevent symlink / mount escapes and TOCTOU races; keep reference inputs read-only;
separate read / write / delete capabilities. A restricted MCP server does not constrain other processes or tools.
Avoids exposing a general host shell.
TypeScript shell semantics · virtual filesystem · selected commands without launching a native host shell
Custom command callbacks remain trusted host-side code; this is not a VM or arbitrary native-process sandbox.
Expose only required commands and virtual paths; audit every custom callback; deny network and host filesystem access
unless explicitly mediated; cap execution time, output size and operation counts. Move risky callbacks into
a separately killable Worker / process with OS enforcement.
Claude Code Sandbox · Anthropic Sandbox Runtime
macOS Seatbelt · Linux bubblewrap / namespaces / seccomp · sandboxed Bash and subprocesses
Allow only task paths; block sensitive home / credential paths; mediate egress through an allowlist proxy;
cover child processes and MCP servers; keep host credentials outside the sandbox; log denied access.
macOS Seatbelt · Linux seccomp + Landlock · Windows sandbox backend / MXC transition
Define workspace write scope and read-only paths; network off or explicitly allowed; constrain subprocesses;
on Windows, test MXC policy translation and desktop / clipboard / input permissions separately.
Cross-platform policy / SDK · Process, Session, WSL and experimental MicroVM containment backends
Declare readable / writable paths, network destinations, environment and UI access; select a supported backend;
test Enforcement / Learning behavior and denied operations. MXC is a policy layer, not one fixed isolation strength.
Containerized shell, tools, dependencies and workspace; long-lived task execution environment
Default container shares the host kernel; OpenHands Runtime is an execution service, not a microVM by itself.
Prefer rootless; drop capabilities; no privileged mode / host socket / unnecessary devices; read-only rootfs;
no-new-privileges; seccomp + AppArmor / SELinux; scoped volumes; cgroup quotas; default-deny egress.
Pod Security Admission · RBAC · NetworkPolicy · CSI / volume policy · runtime selection
RuntimeClass can select gVisor / Kata where installed; a normal Pod is not equivalent to either runtime.
Non-root; no privilege escalation; drop ALL capabilities; read-only rootfs; seccomp RuntimeDefault;
disable ServiceAccount token automount unless needed; default-deny ingress / egress; narrow RBAC;
select and verify RuntimeClass; isolate nodes and storage for mutually untrusted tenants.
User-space kernel (Sentry) · runsc runtime · often deployed behind Docker / Kubernetes RuntimeClass
Use a supported platform and hardened runtime configuration; minimize host mounts and devices; restrict egress;
apply CPU / memory / PID quotas; protect node credentials, runtime sockets and control plane.
Guest kernel · lightweight VM / VMM boundary · per-workload or per-tenant execution
Minimal virtual devices; harden VMM / jailer; use signed immutable images; isolate storage and networking;
block metadata and unintended egress; scope credentials; enforce quotas and destroy task state.
Agent loop managed by Anthropic; execution actions run in customer-controlled sandbox infrastructure
Providers / patterns: Cloudflare · Daytona · Modal · Vercel; Claude session-scoped environments
Harden images; non-root; drop capabilities; read-only rootfs; tenant-bound identity; scoped short-lived credentials;
VPC / firewall egress controls; isolate MCP services; cap resources; clean up session state. Provider isolation
does not replace customer responsibility for image, network and secret policy.
Cloudflare Sandbox · E2B · Modal · Daytona · Vercel Sandbox · AWS Bedrock AgentCore
Managed task sandboxes · code interpreters · API-driven workspaces and execution services
Isolation varies (e.g. gVisor, microVM or container); verify tenant boundary, persistence and lifecycle.
Ephemeral per-task workspace; tenant isolation; short-lived scoped credentials; egress proxy / allowlist;
resource and time budgets; audit execution; revoke grants and destroy workspace at task end.
Dedicated VM · isolated worker pool · Kubernetes-backed sandbox fleet
Bring-your-own execution infrastructure with per-task or per-tenant lifecycle
Isolate queues, storage and network; workload identity; secret broker; signed images; concurrency / cost limits;
reimage or destroy workers; prevent cross-tenant cache, volume and credential reuse.
Agent security runtime · policy enforcement · credential / network mediation · multiple compute backends
Treat the selected backend and its enforcement coverage as the actual isolation boundary.
Default-deny tools and resources; broker short-lived credentials; mediate egress; separate policy administration
from Agent identity; prevent self-modification; record decisions and backend capabilities.
Sandbox API / CRDs · templates, claims, warm pools, runtime adapters and task lifecycle
Control-plane abstractions; select and verify the underlying container, gVisor, Kata or microVM runtime.
Authorize claims; isolate tenant identity, storage and network; enforce quotas and TTL; scrub warm pools;
verify RuntimeClass / backend selection; reconcile orphaned workloads and revoke grants on termination.
WASM / component execution · capability-oriented filesystem, sockets and host imports
Not a drop-in native OS: validate WASI coverage, host imports, escape surface and workload compatibility.
Expose only required WASI interfaces and preopened directories; deny ambient filesystem / network access;
limit fuel / CPU, memory, table and output; validate host functions and component dependencies.
Embedded / lightweight VM-oriented execution for applications and Agent runtimes
Verify host platform, VMM, kernel boundary, device model and project maturity before production use.
Minimize host APIs and virtual devices; isolate VM storage; authenticate control sockets; constrain resources;
patch VMM / guest images; prevent snapshot and cache reuse across tenants.
Fly.io Sprites · Docker Sandboxes / Cloud Sandboxes · Deno Sandbox
Persistent or API-created isolated workspaces · checkpoint / restore · local-to-cloud execution patterns
Product backends and availability vary; do not infer Firecracker / microVM use without verifying deployment.
Encrypt and tenant-bind snapshots; scan restored state; rotate credentials on resume; expire idle workspaces;
prevent poisoned image / cache propagation; audit restore, fork, export and deletion operations.
Browserbase · Steel Browser · Lightpanda · AgentCore Browser
Managed / self-hosted browser sessions and automation-oriented browser runtimes
Browser isolation is not general code isolation; Lightpanda is a browser engine, not a security boundary.
Per-task profiles and cookies; isolate downloads / uploads; restrict navigation and egress; protect credentials;
block local-network and metadata access; mediate clipboard, file chooser, screenshots and user confirmation.

Cross-cutting controls: identity and delegation · policy decision / enforcement points · credential broker · data classification · network egress · quotas · audit · revocation · cleanup. Categories describe distinct concerns, not a single security ranking.
